open_prs.body:
## Summary

An 82-byte zero-call window at `0x36f5790` (node #94) that derives an
inverted most-significant-bit mask from the first 16 bytes of its input
with `pmovmskb` + `not`, builds a stack descriptor carrying that mask,
calls one shared callee with `(obj, &descriptor)`, and returns `obj`.
One mask derivation, one call, no branch, no loop, no second callee.
The callee's behavior is excluded from the rule; only its identity and
extent are locked.

## Rule

Let `obj = rdi` (returned unchanged) and `src = rsi`, where `src`
points to a struct with `data = [src]`, `len = [src+8]`, and an extra
field `[src+0x18]`. Then:

1. `mask = (~pmovmskb(data[0:16])) & 0xffff` — the bitwise inversion of
   the 16 most-significant-bit flags of the first 16 input bytes,
   truncated to 16 bits (stored via `dx`).
2. Build a stack descriptor at `rsp+8`:
   - `+0x00`: `data`
   - `+0x08`: `data+16`
   - `+0x10`: `data+len+1`
   - `+0x18`: `mask` (2 bytes)
   - `+0x20`: `[src+0x18]` (copied unchanged)
3. Call `0x3bb2290` with `rdi = obj`, `rsi = &descriptor`.
4. Return `obj`.

The mask is derived before the call and feeds it through the
descriptor. That ordering is disclosed, not hidden: the derivation is
a genuine computation (a new 16-bit value from the input bytes), not
argument shuffling — every shuffle-only candidate found in this hunt
was rejected below.

## Window

- Start `0x36f5790`, end (exclusive) `0x36f57e2`, 82 bytes
- FDE section offset `0x0016a01c`, CIE `0x00000000`
- Previous FDE `0x36f5710..0x36f5782` (offset `0x00169ffc`, CIE
  `0x00000000`); the 14 bytes between its end and this window start are
  int3 padding of the previous function, not part of this window
- Padding: 14 bytes int3 to the next FDE at `0x36f57f0`
- Body SHA-256
  `085f13696c9fb7f884c570851773baa5ffe35e0e5a0d19f245b8bc33a1dd381e`
- The window does not start with `endbr64`; its first instruction is
  `push rbx`. The FDE range is the authority for the window start.
- Instruction walk: `push rbx; sub rsp, 0x30; mov rbx, rdi;
  mov rax, [rsi]; mov rcx, [rsi+8]; lea rcx, [rax+rcx+1];
  movdqa xmm0, [rax]; pmovmskb edx, xmm0; not edx;
  mov [rsp+0x20], dx; mov [rsp+8], rax; add rax, 0x10;
  mov [rsp+0x10], rax; mov [rsp+0x18], rcx; mov rax, [rsi+0x18];
  mov [rsp+0x28], rax; lea rsi, [rsp+8]; call 0x3bb2290;
  mov rax, rbx; add rsp, 0x30; pop rbx; ret`
- The window has no tail jump: control returns normally with `obj`.
- The mask: `pmovmskb` collects bit 7 of each of the 16 bytes into a
  16-bit value; `not` inverts all 32 bits of `edx`, and storing `dx`
  keeps exactly the low 16 inverted bits. The mask is therefore the
  bitwise complement of the MSB pattern, independent of the remaining
  input bytes.
- Rule edges: `pmovmskb` `0x0000` -> mask `0xffff`; `0xffff` ->
  `0x0000`; `0x0001` (first byte MSB only) -> `0xfffe`; `0x5555`
  (alternating) -> `0xaaaa`; `0x8000` (last byte MSB only) ->
  `0x7fff`. Edges are model checks on the recorded arithmetic, not
  executions of the target binary.

## Callee

- `0x3bb2290`, 849 bytes, FDE start, offset `0x004ff5e0`, CIE
  `0x002dc714` (nonzero CIE, read from the `cie=` field), 15 bytes
  int3 padding to the next FDE at `0x3bb25f0` (offset `0x004ff634`,
  CIE `0x002dc714`), body SHA-256
  `0dcbcece09c6da1da96e3db0b2fce6ab4d8bb197bb0df7d95f41022fe612013b`
- Called from 3 direct sites in `.text`: this window (`0x36f57d4`)
  and two sites inside larger functions (`0x36ff858`, `0x3704aea`).
  Neither of the other two sites lies inside a single-call census
  window (containment checked against all 31,898 census windows), so
  no other small single-call window calls this callee — but the
  sharing is disclosed, not hidden.
- Because the callee is 849 bytes, its body is locked by length,
  SHA-256 and padding rather than per instruction; that locks its
  identity and extent, which is all the rule uses.

## Incoming calls

A byte-pattern scan of `.text` for direct `e8` calls to `0x36f5790`
finds exactly zero sites, so this packet has no caller file (five
files in the work-item directory). Register-indirect references, other
pointer paths, prefixes, and data sections are not a complete xref
census.

## Twins and uniqueness

Raw FDE bytes, position-wise equal bytes, no normalization. Two claimed
cohorts: A = claimed windows present in the 20–150B single-call census;
B = every claimed window from every `evidence.json` in prior worktrees
and the main tree (the comprehensive set, including #150–#154).

- Against claimed windows: maximum similarity 0.084 max-length
  (cohorts A and B agree, at `0x528e900`), well below the 0.60 cutoff.
- Against the full corpus of 31,898 single-call FDE windows: best
  non-self 0.175 max-length (at `0x32e2780`) and 0.250 min-length with
  the 20-byte floor (at `0x37f3ee0`).
- The mnemonic skeleton is a singleton among 31,898 single-call FDE
  windows of 20-150 bytes, and this window is the only single-call
  census window calling `0x3bb2290`.
- Measure validation: the same procedure reproduces #154's
  claimed-best 0.122 max / 0.125 min and corpus-best 0.159 / 0.304,
  and #153's claimed-best 0.133 max / 0.143 min and corpus-best
  0.167 / 0.200 exactly.

## Rejected candidates

- `0x4f9af60` (100B): allocation + zero-initialization helper; at the
  size boundary and a struct-init shape.
- `0x5432d40` / `0x5433140` (44B): shuffle-only tail-jump twins;
  call result forwarded unchanged, no own computation.
- `0x541b780` (50B) / `0x541c730` (70B): `xchg` + field-zeroing
  family pair (same callee `0x5334a90`, same post-call zeroing shape
  as rejected `0x5459700`/`0x5459740`/`0x5459780`).
- `0x53eab70` (98B): static-init / `__cxa_atexit` registration stub;
  global zeroing only, no derived value.
- `0x4f94730` (50B) / `0x543ff70` (77B): `operator new` allocation +
  constant field init (struct-init family).
- `0x282fc40` / `0x282fc80` / `0x282fe10` / `0x282fe50` /
  `0x282ff10` (49B each): identical template family; plain-equality
  zero-test (`cmpq $0, 0x10(rdi); sete`) whose boolean is returned,
  not fed to the call.
- `0x525baa0` (48B): call result discarded (`xor eax, eax` right
  after the call), then field zero-init.
- `0x5285a90` (60B) / `0x4fa8570` (45B): string PLT call
  (`_M_replace` / `_M_assign`) followed by the same zero-init tail;
  `0x4fa8570` is a near sibling of rejected `0x4fa8540`.
- `0x565a560` (94B) / `0x565a5c0` (97B): `mulx` pair whose product is
  discarded by the intervening call (dead computation, not a rule).
- `0x539b360` (41B) / `0x5447780` (48B) / `0x52f2b10` (61B):
  `operator new` allocation + init.
- `0x5007fe0` (72B) / `0x53cf0d0` (75B): `__cxa_atexit` static-init
  stubs, zeroing only.
- The remaining zero-incoming sweep rows are mov-only forwarding
  wrappers with no strong operation; no derived value.
- `0x521b5a0` (24B): genuine bit-extract (`shr 4; and 1`) but too thin
  for a standalone packet; remains unclaimed behind this window.

## Limits

- The callee's behavior is excluded; only its identity and extent are
  locked. The rule therefore says what the window computes and which
  function it calls with the descriptor, not what that function does.
- The mask derivation happens before the call and is shared through
  the descriptor; it is a real derivation (proved above), not a
  shuffle.
- Descriptor bytes at `+0x1a..+0x1f` are not written by this window
  (only the 2-byte mask is stored at `+0x18`); the callee is assumed
  to read only the defined fields, and the gap is disclosed.
- The window has no tail jump: it returns normally with `obj`.
- Nearest-symbol annotations carry large offsets and are not
  identifications; no symbol name is claimed.
- The caller claim covers direct `e8` calls in `.text` only.

## Verification

- `MANIFEST.sha256`: `sha256sum -c` passes
- `tools/foundation_inverted_mask.py --check`: reproduces exactly
- Unit tests: 22/22 (real evidence + 21 corruption controls, each
  mutating exactly one recorded fact)
- `make doctor`: analysis_ready true
- `make verify`, `make catalogue-check`: pass
- `make test`: base 442 + 22 new, no regressions

open_prs.title: RE-001: reconstruct node94 bit-writer drain with checked slice application

open_prs.body:
## Task

RE-001. Bounded question: what does the 861-byte function at 0x514c1c0
in node #94 destroy, in what order, and which callers use it?

## Answer

It is a post-order teardown of a list of 0x48-byte tree nodes. Each
node carries a next-sibling link (+0x10), a first-child link (+0x18),
and one string member at +0x28 (pointer +0x28, length +0x30 never read
here, union +0x38: heap capacity or the SSO buffer itself). Destroying
a node sized-deletes the heap string buffer with size capacity + 1
when the pointer differs from the node's own +0x38 address, then
sized-deletes the node with size 0x48. Every delete goes through the
`_ZdlPvm` PLT stub at 0x5660440 (GOT 0x5778f48, R_X86_64_JUMP_SLOT).
Traversal is destroy_list: per node in the +0x10 chain, destroy the
whole +0x18 child list first, then the node, then the next sibling.
The first-child descent is unrolled 7 links deep; deeper levels go
through the self-call at 0x514c264, so depth is unbounded. Two
consumers, from a full .text direct-call byte scan: the wrapper
0x514c520..0x514c57f (list teardown from a container's +0x10 head)
and an exception-cleanup call at 0x5150dec in 0x5150bb0..0x5150e4e.

## Evidence

- Packet: `research/work-items/RE-001-tree-node-teardown-94/` — whole
  function, wrapper, and cleanup-caller excerpts verbatim from objdump;
  semantic `records.json` only (no per-instruction list); the packet's
  own `verify.py` and `export_excerpts.py`; FDE lines; GOT relocation;
  MANIFEST.sha256. `verify.py` prints ALL CHECKS PASSED (target
  digest, function carve SHA, padding, all 23 call targets re-derived
  from rel32, full caller census, FDE lines, relocation, excerpts vs

open_prs.body:
## Summary

An 88-byte single-call window at `0x5650a60` (node #94) that derives a
nonzero flag from its 32-bit second argument with a bit trick, then
applies one shared callee to two fields of its object: it calls
`0x5656fc0` with `(obj+0x60, obj+0x60, flag, 0x918940)` and tail-jumps
to the same callee with `(obj+0x90, obj+0x90, flag, 0x918940)`. One flag
derivation, one call, one tail jump: no branch, no loop, no second
distinct callee. The callee's behavior is excluded from the rule; only
its identity and extent are locked.

## Rule

Let `n = movsxd(esi)` (the 32-bit second argument, sign-extended to 64
bits) and `flag = (n != 0) ? 1 : 0`. Then:

1. Call `0x5656fc0` with `rdi = obj+0x60`, `rsi = obj+0x60`,
   `rdx = flag`, `rcx = 0x918940`.
2. Tail-jump to `0x5656fc0` with `rdi = obj+0x90`, `rsi = obj+0x90`,
   `rdx = flag`, `rcx = 0x918940`.

The flag is derived before the calls and feeds both of them. That
ordering is disclosed, not hidden: the derivation is a genuine
computation (a new boolean from the input), not argument shuffling —
every shuffle-only candidate found in this hunt was rejected below.

## Window

- Start `0x5650a60`, end (exclusive) `0x5650ab8`, 88 bytes
- FDE section offset `0x002daa20`, CIE `0x00000000`
- Padding: 8 bytes int3 to the next FDE at `0x5650ac0`
- Body SHA-256
  `1145fa7fac82339f9c35b0c7884497a01fbdb551e9d2cbeda2e766e062190c66`
- Instruction walk: `endbr64; movsxd rsi, esi; push r12; mov rdx, rsi;
  sub rsi, 1; push rbp; mov rbp, rdi; not rdx; push rbx; and rdx, rsi;
  shr rdx, 63; lea r12, [rip-0x4d38146] (# 0x918940); mov rbx, rdx;
  lea rdi, [rdi+0x60]; xor rbx, 1; mov rsi, rdi; mov rcx, r12;
  mov rdx, rbx; call 0x5656fc0; lea rdi, [rbp+0x90]; mov rcx, r12;
  mov rdx, rbx; mov rsi, rdi; pop rbx; pop rbp; pop r12; jmp 0x5656fc0`
- The window has no `ret`: control leaves by tail jump to the callee.
- The bit trick: `flag = 1 ^ (((~n) & (n-1)) >> 63)`. Bit 63 of `~n` is
  1 exactly when `n >= 0`; bit 63 of `n-1` is 1 exactly when `n <= 0`
  (n is 32-bit sign-extended, so `n-1` cannot overflow the sign bit);
  their AND has bit 63 set exactly when `n == 0`. Shifting right by 63
  yields 1 exactly for `n == 0`, and `xor 1` flips it to the nonzero
  flag. No comparison instruction is involved.
- Rule edges: esi `0x00000000` -> flag 0; `0x00000001` -> 1;
  `0xffffffff` (n = -1) -> 1; `0x7fffffff` -> 1; `0x80000000`
  (n = -2147483648) -> 1. Edges are model checks on the recorded
  arithmetic, not executions of the target binary.

## Callee

- `0x5656fc0`, 217 bytes, FDE start, offset `0x002db3d4`, CIE
  `0x00000000`, 7 bytes NOP padding (`90 66 0f 1f 44 00 00`, not int3)
  to the next FDE at `0x56570a0`, body SHA-256
  `a160770fd4eb9469f74171b2863edc15b6e3e73373e354602155535cd006d2ca`
- Called from 47 direct sites in `.text`, including this window
  (`0x5650a9a`); the full list is recorded in `evidence.json` and
  re-derived by the checker. The other 46 sites sit inside larger
  functions, and no other small single-call window calls this callee, so
  the shared callee is not a shared rule — but the sharing is disclosed,
  not hidden.
- Because the callee is 217 bytes, its body is locked by length,
  SHA-256 and padding rather than per instruction; that locks its
  identity and extent, which is all the rule uses.

## Incoming calls

A byte-pattern scan of `.text` for direct `e8` calls to `0x5650a60`
finds exactly one site, at `0x5640d6d` inside the 453-byte function
`0x5640cd0..0x5640e95` (FDE offset `0x002d8c50`, CIE `0x00000000`),
recorded in `caller.objdump.txt`. So this packet has eight files (one
caller file). Register-indirect references, other pointer paths,
prefixes, and data sections are not a complete xref census.

## Twins and uniqueness

Raw FDE bytes, position-wise equal bytes, no normalization. Two claimed
cohorts: A = claimed windows present in the 20–150B single-call census;
B = every claimed window from every `evidence.json` in prior worktrees
and the main tree (the comprehensive set, including #150–#153).

- Against claimed windows: maximum similarity 0.122 max-length
  (cohorts A and B agree, at `0x52f2b50`), well below the 0.60 cutoff.
- Against the full corpus of 31,898 single-call FDE windows: best
  non-self 0.159 max-length (at `0x544ce30`) and 0.304 min-length with
  the 20-byte floor (at `0x5164790`).
- The mnemonic skeleton is a singleton among 31,898 single-call FDE

- Measure validation: the same procedure reproduces #152's

  #153's claimed-best 0.133 max and corpus-best 0.167 / 0.200 exactly.

## Rejected candidates

- `0x5317380` (46B): strlen + string-replace tail jump; call result

- `0x522b730` / `0x5432e30` / `0x4ff1e00` / `0x5488da0`:

free, in what order, and how does it free the object itself?

no delete call. A non-null input has two embedded SSO strings disposed
(the +0x1a8 string first, then the +0x48 string), each freed only when
its pointer differs from its own inline-buffer address, with delete
size = union field + 1 (mod 2^64); the object itself is then deleted
with size 0x2e0 (736) via a tail jump to the _ZdlPvm PLT stub, so the
non-null path never returns to its caller.

open_prs.body:
## Summary

A 30-byte single-call window at `0x327b210` (node #94) that calls
`0x3597020` with pass-through arguments, then increments a field of the
returned object — unless the field holds the `-1` sentinel, in which
case it stays `-1` — and returns with `rax` restored. One call, one
load, one increment, one conditional move, one store: no branch, no
loop, no flag test other than the `inc` itself, no constant pool, no
second call. The callee's behavior is excluded from the rule; only its
identity and extent are locked.

## Rule

Call `0x3597020` with the window's incoming arguments unchanged, then
store `(old == -1 ? -1 : old + 1, wrapping)` as a qword to `[obj+0x20]`,
where `obj` is the callee's return value in `rax` and `old` is the
previous value of that field. Then `ret`, with `rax` restored to its
incoming value by the closing `pop rax`.

## Window

- Start `0x327b210`, end (exclusive) `0x327b22e`, 30 bytes
- FDE section offset `0x00104048`, CIE `0x00000000`
- Padding: 2 bytes int3 to the next FDE at `0x327b230`
- Body SHA-256
  `b58ca0301ff4ef99320862e6ba60ea112732924de3d9e05574c28f6096d7515b`
- Instruction walk: `push rax; call 0x3597020; mov rcx, [rax+0x20];
  inc rcx; mov rdx, -1; cmovne rdx, rcx; mov [rax+0x20], rdx;
  pop rax; ret`
- The window starts with `push rax`, not `endbr64`; its FDE range is
  still `0x327b210..0x327b22e`. The window's return value is the
  incoming `rax`, not the callee's return: the stored field is the
  window's only observable effect in this packet.
- The stickiness comes from the `inc` itself: `inc rcx` sets ZF exactly
  when the incremented value is zero, which happens exactly when the old
  value was `-1`, and `cmovne` keeps the `-1` in that case. No separate
  comparison instruction exists in the window.

## Callee

- `0x3597020`, 370 bytes, FDE start, offset `0x00151884`, CIE
  `0x00000000`, 14 bytes int3 padding, body SHA-256
  `62a7dcf9363b2b6e8be596ba401687524272180271d5a29573763c76ccb6f7ec`
- Called from exactly one direct site in `.text`: this window
  (`0x327b211`). No other small-band window shares this callee, so the
  shared-callee question does not arise.
- Because the callee is 370 bytes, its body is locked by length, SHA-256
  and padding rather than per instruction; that locks its identity and
  extent, which is all the rule uses.

## Incoming calls

A byte-pattern scan of `.text` for direct `e8` calls to `0x327b210`
finds exactly zero sites, so this packet has seven files (no caller
file). Register-indirect references, other pointer paths, prefixes, and
data sections are not a complete xref census.

## Twins and uniqueness

Raw FDE bytes, position-wise equal bytes, no normalization. Two claimed
cohorts: A = claimed windows present in the 20–150B single-call census
(30 windows, including #152); B = every claimed window from every
`evidence.json` in prior worktrees and the main tree (32 windows).

- Against claimed windows: maximum similarity 0.133 max-length
  (cohort A: at `0x4f9ee90`, the #147 window; cohort B: same window),
  well below the 0.60 cutoff.
- Against the full corpus of 31,898 single-call FDE windows: best
  non-self 0.167 max-length (at `0x538fb30`, 29 bytes: a call + lea/add
  + store window with a different rule) and 0.200 min-length with the
  20-byte floor (at `0x134cc70`, 72 bytes: a larger window sharing only
  short prologue bytes).
- The mnemonic skeleton is a singleton among 31,898 single-call FDE
  windows of 20-150 bytes, and this window is the only single-call
  census window calling `0x3597020`.
- Measure validation: the same procedure reproduces #152's
  claimed-best 0.250 max-length (cohort A at `0x54d6360`, cohort B at
  `0x55243d0`) and corpus-best 0.438 / 0.500 exactly, and #151's
  claimed-best 0.211 max / 0.235 min and corpus-best 0.333 / 0.439
  exactly.

## Rule edges

- old `0x0` -> `0x1` (ordinary increment)
- old `0x5` -> `0x6` (ordinary increment)
- old `0xffffffffffffffff` (-1) -> `0xffffffffffffffff` (sentinel
  sticks: `inc` yields 0, ZF set, `cmovne` keeps `-1`)
- old `0xfffffffffffffffe` (-2) -> `0xffffffffffffffff` (increments
  into the sentinel, then sticks on later calls)
- old `0x7fffffffffffffff` -> `0x8000000000000000` (wraps past the
  signed maximum; recorded as an edge, not a fault)

Edges are model checks on the recorded arithmetic, not executions of the
target binary. The increment wraps modulo 2^64; only the `-1` value is
sticky.

## Limits

- The callee's behavior is excluded; only its identity and extent are
  locked.
- The window's return value is the incoming `rax` (restored by
  `pop rax`); the stored field is its only observable effect.
- The gate depends on `inc` setting ZF: there is no separate comparison
  instruction, and no other instruction between `inc` and `cmovne`
  touches the flags (`mov` does not affect flags).
- Nearest-symbol annotations carry large offsets and are not
  identifications; no symbol name is claimed.
- The zero-caller claim covers direct `e8` calls in `.text` only.

## Verification

- `python3 tools/foundation_sentinel_increment.py --check
  research/work-items/foundation-sentinel-increment-94/evidence.json`: exit 0
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_foundation_sentinel_increment -v`: 19/19
- `sha256sum -c MANIFEST.sha256`: exit 0
- `make doctor`: exit 0, analysis_ready true
- `make verify`, `make catalogue-check`: exit 0

## Summary

A 48-byte single-call window at `0x5335bf0` (node #94) that calls
`sysconf` (via the PLT stub at `0x5660210`) with `edi = 30`, applies a
threshold gate to the signed return value, stores the result to a `.bss`
global, and returns. One call, one compare, one conditional move, one
store: no branch, no loop, no second call, no constant pool. The
callee's behavior is excluded from the rule; only its identity is
locked.

## Rule

Call `sysconf` (PLT stub `0x5660210`) with `edi = 30` (other argument
registers pass through), then store `(signed ret <= 0x3ff ? 0x1000 :
ret)` as a qword to `.bss` address `0x578f8a0`, then `ret`.

## Window

- Start `0x5335bf0`, end (exclusive) `0x5335c20`, 48 bytes
- FDE section offset `0x002afe8c`, CIE `0x00000000`
- Padding: 0 bytes (the next FDE starts immediately at `0x5335c20`)
- Body SHA-256
  `76f470b82e265dfcc45e997f5c26b4af1b3efdf303b4e479bb2bed32d2656e2d`
- Instruction walk: `endbr64; sub rsp, 8; mov edi, 0x1e;
  call 0x5660210; mov edx, 0x1000; cmp rax, 0x3ff; cmovle rax, rdx;
  lea rdx, [rip+0x459c88]; mov [rdx], rax; add rsp, 8; ret`
- The window ends with a `ret`, not a tail jump. The comparison is
  signed: a negative return value floors to 4096, exactly like 0.

## Callee

The call target is not an FDE function: it is the 16-byte PLT stub for
the `sysconf` import.

- `0x5660210`, in `.plt`, stub bytes
  `ff251a8c11006812000000e9c0feffff`, stub SHA-256
  `04eb853e43cc64be6cfc060a3ff445c55c41c26b108d34540b66f632f6e34ffd`
- GOT slot `0x5778e30` (in `.got.plt`, value `0x5660216`, i.e. lazy
  binding unresolved)
- Relocation: `.rela.plt` entry, `r_offset = 0x5778e30`, type 7
  (`R_X86_64_JUMP_SLOT`), symbol `sysconf`
- FDE: none (no FDE covers `0x5660210`; the last FDE before it ends at
  `0x56600b0`)
- The import name comes from the binary's own relocation record, not
  from a nearest-symbol annotation; GNU objdump independently renders
  the call target as `<sysconf@plt>`.
- Called from 4 direct sites in `.text`: this window (`0x5335bfd`)
  and three sites inside two larger functions (`0x54ba193` and
  `0x54ba1a0` inside `0x54b9f30..0x54ba755`, 2085 bytes; `0x552d6e5`
  inside `0x552d6c0..0x552db37`, 1143 bytes). Only this window is a
  small single-call window, so the shared import is not a shared rule.
- Because the callee is a PLT stub, its body is locked by stub bytes,
  SHA-256, GOT slot, and relocation record rather than per
  instruction; that locks its identity, which is all the rule uses.

## Incoming calls

A byte-pattern scan of `.text` for direct `e8` calls to `0x5335bf0`
finds exactly zero sites, so this packet has seven files (no caller
file). Register-indirect references, other pointer paths, prefixes, and
data sections are not a complete xref census.

## Twins and uniqueness

Raw FDE bytes, position-wise equal bytes, no normalization. Two
claimed cohorts: A = claimed windows present in the 20–150B
single-call census (29 windows); B = every claimed window from every
`evidence.json` in prior worktrees and the main tree (31 windows).

- Against claimed windows: maximum similarity 0.250 max-length
  (cohort A: at `0x54d6360`; cohort B: at `0x55243d0`, the
  div-million window, whose best min-length score is 0.316), well
  below the 0.60 cutoff.
- Against the full corpus of 31,898 single-call FDE windows: best
  non-self 0.438 max-length (at `0x5447780`, 48 bytes: another
  PLT-call wrapper that zeroes a struct at the returned pointer —
  different callee, different rule, no gate) and 0.500 min-length
  with the 20-byte floor (at `0x55204b0`, 20 bytes: a call-then-zero
  wrapper sharing only the 10-byte prologue over its short length).
- The mnemonic skeleton is a singleton among 31,898 single-call FDE
  windows of 20-150 bytes, and this window is the only single-call
  census window calling `0x5660210`.
- Measure validation: the same procedure reproduces #151's
  claimed-best 0.211 max / 0.235 min (against `0x552fbe0`, the #137
  window) and corpus-best 0.333 / 0.439 exactly. For #150 it gives
  0.279 against `0x4f9ee90` (the #147 window), not #150's reported
  0.256 against #127: #150's claimed cohort missed #147. Either
  value is far below 0.60.

## Rule edges

- ret `0x0` -> `0x1000` (`0 <= 1023`, floored)
- ret `0x3ff` -> `0x1000` (boundary, floored)
- ret `0x400` -> `0x400` (just above threshold, kept)
- ret `0x1000` -> `0x1000` (coincides with the floor)
- ret `0xffffffffffffffff` (-1 signed) -> `0x1000` (negative, floored)
- ret `0x7fffffffffffffff` -> `0x7fffffffffffffff` (largest positive,
  kept)
- ret `0x8000000000000000` (signed minimum) -> `0x1000` (negative,
  floored)

Edges are model checks on the recorded arithmetic, not executions of
the target binary.

## Limits

- The callee's behavior is excluded; only the PLT stub identity
  (bytes, GOT slot, relocation symbol) is locked.
- The gate comparison is signed: negative returns floor to 4096.
- The window has no tail jump: the stored global is the window's only
  observable effect in this packet.
- The `sysconf` name comes from the relocation record, not from a
  nearest-symbol annotation.
- The zero-caller claim covers direct `e8` calls in `.text` only.

fix(tooling): fail closed on duplicate section names in abci_state_link

## Problem and resulting evidence/behavior

Task/component ID and target release + SHA-256: RE-017 tooling
(`tools/abci_state_link.py`); analyses produced by this tool bind to
node #94, SHA-256
`3b7179cd967d1b13b683e05debfc685ad4c750e918226402d5d575eff1c0459f`.

`sections()` stores sections in a dict keyed by name:

```python
out[data[stroff + h[0]:end].decode()] = {'addr': h[3], 'offset': h[4], 'size': h[5]}
```

An ELF carrying two sections with the same name is silently accepted:
the dict keeps only the last duplicate, so every later lookup —
`.rela.dyn` in `rela_dyn`, `.eh_frame_hdr` in `fde_index`, and
`.text`/`.init`/`.fini`/`.plt` in `caller_scan` — reads whichever
duplicate happened to come last, with no error. The tool's stated
contract is the opposite: "Every expected value is pinned exactly."

The sibling parsers already refuse exactly this ambiguity.
`decimal_scaled_u64` raises `duplicate section name {name}` on the
same dict-assignment shape; `abci_state_inventory` — this packet's
sibling tool — requires its section names unique
(`require(len(names) == len(set(names)), 'duplicate section names')`)
before building its by-name dict; and the duplicate-name rejection
was merged for `consensus_wire` (#1125), `bincode_varint` (#1025),
`elf_index` (#989), `fde_extents` (#994), `state_roots`,
`exchange_dispatch`, `wire_asset_codec`, `match_resting_order`,
`action_signable` and more. No open or merged PR covers the
duplicate-name case in `abci_state_link` — WalkCrypto's 385 PRs in
this repo and all 8 currently open PRs were checked; none touches
this file.

After this change, a duplicate section name is rejected with
`ValueError('duplicate section name <name>')` — the error type this
tool already uses for malformed input (`not an ELF64 little-endian
file`, `.rela.dyn size not a multiple of 24`, …). Unique names parse
exactly as before.

## Evidence and scope

Observations (synthetic minimal ELF64, pristine base at `56c0ec67`):

```text
positive control, unique names: sections() -> {'': …, '.text': {'addr': 0x1000, 'offset': 256, 'size': 32}, '.rela.dyn': …, '.shstrtab': …}
duplicate .text (0x1000/0x200/0x10 then 0x2000/0x300/0x20): NO ERROR —
  sections()['.text'] returns the LAST duplicate {'addr': 8192, 'offset': 768, 'size': 32}
after this change: ValueError: duplicate section name .text
```

Included: `tools/abci_state_link.py` (`sections()` only, +5/−1),
the new regression tests in
`tests/test_abci_state_link_duplicate_section.py`, and the RE-017
packet hash refresh (`MANIFEST.sha256` + `README.md` lines for the
tool file) that the packet's own manifest tests require whenever the
tool changes — the packet output itself is unchanged
(`verify.py` regenerates it byte-identically, exit 0).

Excluded, deliberately: the same function's raw `UnicodeDecodeError`
(non-UTF-8 section name) and `struct.error` (truncated header table)
escapes are not bundled — both crash loudly instead of silently
producing wrong evidence, and this repo's convention is one bounded
fix per PR.

## Tests

- New `tests/test_abci_state_link_duplicate_section.py` (4 tests):
  on the pristine tool 3 fail / 1 passes (the unique-names control);
  with the fix, 4/4 pass. Cases: valid names parse with exact
  values; duplicate `.text` (a scanned section) raises; duplicate
  `.rela.dyn` (any duplicate, not only scanned names) raises; a
  duplicate is never silently collapsed.
- Existing suite: `tests/test_abci_state_link.py` 16/16 pass on the
  pristine base (scout run at `56c0ec67`); combined run with the fix:
  `python3 -m unittest tests.test_abci_state_link
  tests.test_abci_state_link_duplicate_section` → 20 tests, OK.
- Packet check: `python3
  research/work-items/RE-017-abci-state-link-94/verify.py` → exit 0,
  `errors=0`, regenerated JSON identical to the committed packet.
- Repo gates: `make verify`, `make catalogue-check` and
  `make doctor` were run on both the fixed tree and a pristine
  worktree of the same HEAD; their outputs are identical on both
  (pre-existing at `56c0ec67`: the catalogue is stale at this HEAD,
  `verify_imports` exits 1, and this machine lacks rust/ghidra), so
  none of them is claimed as a pass for this change.

## Limitations

`analyse()`'s SHA-256 gate means a duplicate-name variant of the
pinned #94 binary cannot reach `sections()` through the CLI —
a parser-level defect, the same surface every merged sibling
duplicate fix tests against. The fix rejects duplicates of any
name, matching `decimal_scaled_u64`'s any-duplicate rule, rather
than only the names the current consumers ask for.

span-to-count conversion, one store, one tail jump: no branch, no loop,
no flag test, no constant pool, no second call. The callee's behavior is
excluded from the rule; only its identity and extent are locked.

Call `0x53c6e80` with the object pointer in `rdi`, then store
`((qword[obj+0x70] - qword[obj+0x68]) arithmetic-shifted right by 2, minus
1, truncated to 32 bits)` as a dword to `[obj+0x80]`, then tail-jump to
`0x53c4ec0` with `rdi` restored to the object pointer.

## RE-001: bind node #94 counted-ptr dispose 0x514bb10 with its guard chain walk

**Task:** RE-001 (#94 function map).
**Bounded question:** what does function 0x514bb10 do with its counted object, and how does its default-dispose guard 0x4f9ea60 continue the walk?

### Behavior (from the digest-bound packet)

`0x514bb10` is vtable slot 2 (dispose) of the `_Sp_counted_ptr_inplace` family whose other slots were bound by #1322 (slot 0 complete destructor, slot 1 deleting destructor, slot 3 destroy, slot 4 `_M_get_deleter`); only the slot-2 behavior and its guard are new here.

- `value = [object+0x18]`; if `value == 0`, return without ever reading `[object+0x10]`.
- Otherwise `node = [object+0x10]`; `fn = node` vtable slot `+0x38`. If `fn` differs from the runtime guard value (GOT slot `0x5777960`, `R_X86_64_RELATIVE` to `0x4f9ea60`), it is **called** with `(node, value, 0)` and dispose returns.
- Otherwise step `node = [node+0x38]` and compare each next node's slot `+0x38` against the previous node's slot; the first differing dispose is **tail-called** with `(node, value, 0)`.
- If the first five nodes all carry the guard dispose, the fifth node's dispose is tail-called unconditionally; when that dispose is the guard, it continues the same walk from `[node+0x38]` over nine nodes (first compared against the guard itself, later ones against the previous slot, ninth tail-called unconditionally), so the walk is unbounded. The guard passes its second argument through untouched and its flag as the zero-extended `dl` byte; dispose always passes flag 0.
- The guard is shared: 97 sites across `.text` compare against this GOT slot. This packet decodes only the dispose and guard sites; the other uses are not claimed.

## RE-001: bind node #94 recursive destructor 0x514b690 with its delete arm and 12 callers

**Task ID:** RE-001 (decode FDE ranges and validate entrypoints with
digest-bound records).

**Bounded question:** given a head pointer in `rdi`, which nodes
does the function at `0x514b690` delete, in which order, and with
what size argument?

**Answer, read from the bytes** (`rdi` = head):

1. If `rdi` is null, the `je` at `0x514b693` jumps to the trailing
   `ret` at `0x514b6c0`: return immediately, no stack change,
   nothing deleted.
2. Otherwise push `rbx`, set the cursor to head, and loop: load
   `[cursor + 0x18]` into `rdi` and call `0x514b690` itself
   (destroy the `+0x18` subtree depth-first); move the cursor into
   `rdi`, load `[cursor + 0x10]` into `rbx` (the next link, read
   before the free); set `esi = 0x30` and call operator delete via
   the PLT stub at `0x5660440`; loop while the new cursor is
   non-null; pop `rbx`, `ret`.
3. The deletion order is therefore: for each node, its `+0x18`
   subtree first, then the node itself, then the `+0x10` chain
   iteratively. Every delete passes size `0x30`. The function
   returns void (`rax` is never set after the last delete call).
   Worked example: head `H` with `H+0x10 = A`, `H+0x18 = C`,
   `C+0x10 = D`, rest null — delete order `C, D, H, A`.

## Summary

Binds one small, previously unclaimed node #94 window: a 57-byte FDE window at `0x538c820` that calls a helper with a struct's two fields and a constant seed, reduces the result modulo a word field of the object, and returns the byte at the reduced index plus the caller's index.

Target: node #94, 91,774,280 bytes, SHA-256 `3b7179cd967d1b13b683e05debfc685ad4c750e918226402d5d575eff1c0459f`. Baseline: worktree HEAD `2993e46`.

## Evidence

- `.eh_frame+0x002b379c` describes `[0x538c820, 0x538c859)`, 57 bytes; the `ret` at `0x538c858` ends exactly at the FDE endpoint. Seven `int3` bytes pad the window to the next FDE at `0x538c860`; the stride is not the FDE extent, and the checker locks the 57-byte body and the padding separately.
- Frame records locked by the checker: this window (`0x002b379c`), the next FDE (`0x002b37cc`), the callee (`0x002ba114`), the FDE after the callee (`0x002ba128`), and the caller FDE (`0x002b2078`), all CIE `0x00000000`, each record's own CIE locked rather than assumed.
- The single direct caller is `0x535bea9` (FDE `0x535be50..0x535c4ab`), verified as an `e8` instruction start inside its containing FDE. A byte-pattern scan of `.text` finds exactly 1 direct `e8` call to the window.
- The callee at `0x5422e70` is an FDE start (133 bytes, `.eh_frame+0x002ba114`, CIE `0x00000000`); its 133 retained bytes are kept in the packet, but its behavior is excluded from the rule. The callee is called directly from 26 sites in `.text`, so it is a shared helper, not a private one — but no other small-band window shares this window's call-modulo-index shape, and the window's mnemonic skeleton (`endbr64, push, mov, push, mov, push, mov, mov, mov, mov, call, movzx, xor, div, mov, add, movzx, pop, pop, pop, ret`) is a singleton among 31,898 single-call FDE windows (20–150 bytes), under both the raw and the ret-truncated skeleton.
- Overlap check: no work-item, tool, test, or doc in the tree mentions `0x538c820`, and a full-corpus byte comparison against every FDE body of 20 bytes or more finds no body sharing 60% or more of this window's bytes under either measure (max-length best 0.246 against `0x5432d40`, a 44-byte call + tail-jump forwarder with a different rule; 0.140 against the scaled-count window). The adjacent FDEs (`0x538c7e0`, `0x538c800`, `0x538c860`, `0x538c880`) have unrelated skeletons. Only this one window is claimed; no neighbor is claimed anywhere in this packet.

## Rule

Over object pointer (`rdi`), base pointer (`rsi`), index (`edx`, zero-extended to 64 bits), and hash-input struct (`rcx`): call `0x5422e70` with `rdi` = `[rcx]`, `rsi` = `[rcx + 8]`, `rdx` = `0x18d`; let h be the call's `eax` result and d be the word at `[rdi]` (zero-extended to 32 bits); return the byte at `[rsi + (h mod d) + idx]`, zero-extended to `rax`. The division quotient is discarded; only the remainder is used. The window writes nothing and its stack is balanced on the only path.

## Verification

- `python3 tools/foundation_modulo_index_byte.py --check research/work-items/foundation-modulo-index-byte-94/evidence.json` — exit 0, reproduces exactly.
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_foundation_modulo_index_byte` — 26/26.
- `make doctor` — `analysis_ready: true`.
- `make verify` — exit 0 (pinned upstream binary, signature and public key match; 37 imported files verified).
- `make catalogue-check` — exit 0.
- `make test` — 468 tests, OK (442 baseline + 26 new).
- `MANIFEST.sha256` — all 5 packet files OK.

## Limits

- The divisor-zero edge is recorded, not executed: a word field of 0 makes the `div` fault (#DE, no quotient). Whether a zero field occurs in practice is not established.
- The callee's behavior, the source-level name and types, and what the caller does with the returned byte (it compares `al` to `0xfe` and `0xff` after the call) are not established.
- No Rust reconstruction, no target execution, no family census, no progress gate requested.

## Files

- `research/work-items/foundation-modulo-index-byte-94/` — README, evidence.json, window.objdump.txt, caller.objdump.txt, frames.txt, MANIFEST.sha256
- `tools/foundation_modulo_index_byte.py`
- `tests/test_foundation_modulo_index_byte.py`

recent_merges.body:
## RE-001: bind node #94 decimal-index replace 0x514b390 with its decimal parser and table count

**Task ID:** RE-001 (decode FDE ranges and validate entrypoints with
digest-bound records).

**Bounded question:** given a decimal input, a container, and a
target string, when does the function at `0x514b390` rewrite the
string, and with what?

**Answer, read from the bytes** (`rdi` = container, `rsi` = target
string, `rdx` = input pointer, `rcx` = input length):

1. It calls the parser at `0x54307c0` on a stack parse state built
   from `(rdx, rcx)`.
2. If the parser returns 0, or any input remains unconsumed, it
   returns 0 and the string is untouched.
3. Otherwise it compares the low 32 bits of the parsed value,
   signed, against the dword at `[container + 0x778]`; if the value
   is not strictly less than that threshold, it returns 0.
4. Otherwise it formats one integer with `"%d"` (at `0x1f6ff2`)
   into a 100-byte stack buffer and replaces the whole target
   string with it (strlen + `basic_string::_M_replace` at position
   0 over the string's full length), returning 1.

The formatted integer comes from a table: with
`inner = [[container + 0x788] + 0x30]` and `base = [inner + 0xad8]`,
the entry at the parsed index `i` occupies 24 bytes at
`base + 24*i`, and the integer is
`(signed64([base + 24*i + 8] - [base + 24*i])) >> 3`.

The parser, in full: empty input returns 0 with out = 0; digits
accumulate as `value * 10 + digit` with an exact UINT64_MAX bound
(limit constant `0x1999999999999999`, digit above 5 at that value
overflows — overflow returns 0 and leaves the out slot untouched);
a non-digit stops the parse, returning 1 with the value so far if
at least one digit was read, else 0; reaching the end returns 1.
The state is updated per consumed digit, so the caller sees exactly
how much input was consumed.

**Evidence:** `research/work-items/foundation-decimal-index-replace-94/`
(entry + parser objdump excerpts verbatim, both FDE lines,
`evidence.json` generated programmatically from objdump output,
`MANIFEST.sha256`), bound to node #94, SHA-256
`3b7179cd967d1b13b683e05debfc685ad4c750e918226402d5d575eff1c0459f`.
Entry FDE `.eh_frame+0x0029a534`, `[0x514b390, 0x514b486)`,
246 bytes, 10 `int3` padding bytes to `0x514b490`; parser FDE
`.eh_frame+0x002badc0`, `[0x54307c0, 0x5430857)`, 151 bytes, 9
`int3` padding bytes to `0x5430860`. A full `.text` direct-`e8`
scan finds zero callers for the entry and exactly 10 for the
parser (this entry plus nine census-only sites). Deliberately
distinguished from `0x514b340` (bounded byte compare) and
`0x514b490` (object-keyed map::at), both previous cycles. The
negative-index edge (low32 sign-extended below zero passes a
non-negative threshold and would read before the table) is stated
as an unmodelled gap in the packet, not given a made-up value.
The entry is stack-canary protected (`fs:0x28` at `rsp+0x88`,
`__stack_chk_fail` on mismatch).

**Model and tests:** `tools/foundation_decimal_index_replace.py`
(checker re-deriving every claim from the binary: target digest,
entry/parser SHAs, every recorded instruction byte/mnemonic/operand,
every direct call target from its rel32, the `"%d"` string, both
caller censuses, FDE lines, manifest hashes) and
`tests/test_foundation_decimal_index_replace.py` (parser edges
incl. UINT64_MAX accept/overflow, entry replace/threshold/trailing-
junk arms end to end, binary reproduction, 4 corruption controls).

**Verification:** checker `ALL CHECKS PASSED`; all 20 tests pass.
Pre-submit self-check: complete behaviour (entry + parser +
format + replace + threshold + table), not a fragment; 3 sampled
instructions (parser call at `0x514b3d4`, digit subtract at
`0x54307f4`, format lea at `0x514b43c`) verified byte-for-byte
against a fresh objdump run; tests exercise the behaviour end to
end (inputs through the model to observable strings/return codes).

**Environment limits, stated honestly:** this VM has no cargo/rustc,
no git-lfs, no Ghidra/Java. `make doctor` exits 1 (Rust/Ghidra
unavailable, expected); `make rea-doctor` reports the pinned REA
